summary.text: 个 is used today mainly as a general classifier for individual people and things. Traditional accounts associate the related forms 箇 and 个 with bamboo, and report 个 as an alternate form meaning half a bamboo; they do not establish a complete graphic path to the modern character.

formation.text: Treat 个 as a whole graph. The transmitted analysis of related 箇 has 竹 for the bamboo category and 固 as a sound element. A commentary reports 个 as an alternate form meaning half a bamboo, but this does not establish that the modern classifier was borrowed from the spoken name of a bamboo object.

components.text: Read 个 here as a whole graph. A proposed breakdown into a tally and a person is not established as its historical construction.

In the related graph 箇, the transmitted analysis assigns 竹 the bamboo category. The curated seal-script-style image shows 竹 above 固; it illustrates this analysis, not a dated stage in 个’s graphic history.

In 箇, the transmitted analysis identifies 固 as the sound element. The cited Old Chinese forms for 固 and 箇 are similar but not identical; this comparison does not establish the spoken name of a bamboo object.

sound_limitation.text: The cited comparison gives a Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese form for 箇 and a reported form for 固, but no directly verified same-system reading for 固. The comparison supports reported similarity, not independent proof of the analysis or a bamboo object’s name.

sound.text: The reported Old Chinese forms are similar but not identical; the comparison is compatible with a sound relationship but does not independently verify the component analysis.

history.text: The curated image is a modern redraw of 箇 in a transmitted Shuowen seal-script style, with 竹 above 固. It illustrates the traditional analysis rather than a securely dated stage in 个’s graphic history.

A transmitted lexicographic account reports 个 as an alternate form meaning half a bamboo, while a variant dictionary catalogs 个 as a variant of 個. These accounts do not document a complete graphic sequence linking 箇, 個 and modern 个.

uncertainties.text: The cited records do not establish an oracle-bone or bronze form for 个, or a dated graphic path from the bamboo-related account to modern 个. This does not show that earlier forms never existed.

Bamboo-related and ritual counting uses are recorded, but their chronology and a continuous development into the general classifier are unresolved. A research abstract proposes a more complex history.
No independently recoverable spoken name for the proposed bamboo object is available here. Similar reported readings make sound-based borrowing possible, but do not demonstrate it.

senses.text: A transmitted commentary reports this meaning for 个 as an alternate form; it is not established as the character’s earliest meaning.
A cited classical passage is associated by commentary with counting bamboo. It does not establish the first attestation or a transition to the general classifier.

senses.gloss: counting item or unit, like 枚
senses.text: A ritual counting context is recorded, with 个 glossed as comparable to 枚. The available evidence does not date this sense or connect it to bamboo-related counting.

senses.gloss: general classifier for individual people or things
senses.text: 个 is used as a general classifier for counting people and objects. Its emergence is not dated here.
A current sense meaning “single” or “individual” is recorded. Its historical relation to the classifier is not established here.

limitations.text: The recorded historical counting uses cannot be placed in a secure sequence, and no semantic bridge from bamboo-related counting to general classifier use is established; no development is asserted.
Modern dictionaries also record demonstrative and particle uses, but no dated sequence connects them to the older counting uses.
